classification.difficultyReason: Construct intersecting lines, measure their four angles and match the opposite pairs to check the stated equality rule.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw two lines, $AB$ and $PQ$, intersecting at $O$.

answer.short: Sample construction shown. Other intersecting lines are possible.
answer.worked: Draw a straight line through $A$, $O$ and $B$. Draw a second straight line through $P$, $O$ and $Q$, with $O$ between $P$ and $Q$.

spec.description: Authored sample construction: two straight lines AB and PQ intersect at O. The source supplies no fixed angle or diagram.
spec.mathematics: A, O and B are collinear; P, O and Q are collinear. The sample has angle POB equal to 60 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student must draw their own intersecting lines.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Measure the sizes of $\angle AOP$, $\angle POB$, $\angle BOQ$ and $\angle QOA$.

answer.short: For the sample: $\angle AOP=120^\circ$, $\angle POB=60^\circ$, $\angle BOQ=120^\circ$, $\angle QOA=60^\circ$. Answers depend on the construction.
answer.worked:
Place the protractor centre at $O$ and align its baseline with an arm of each angle. Read the scale starting at $0^\circ$ on that arm. For the sample construction:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOP&=120^\circ\\\angle POB&=60^\circ\\\angle BOQ&=120^\circ\\\angle QOA&=60^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Check that they obey the statement, ‘Vertically opposite angles are equal’.

answer.short: $\angle AOP=\angle BOQ$ and $\angle POB=\angle QOA$, allowing for measurement accuracy.
answer.worked:
Compare the angles opposite each other across $O$. For the sample:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOP&=\angle BOQ=120^\circ\\\angle POB&=\angle QOA=60^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Both vertically opposite pairs are equal. Measurements from other constructions should also agree within measurement accuracy.
